title: Advanced Finance
completion_message: ¡Excelente! Hablar de dinero a nivel corporativo no se trata solo de ingresos y gastos. Ahora conoces la jerga de Wall Street, los rescates financieros y cómo se mueve el capital en el mundo.

parts.visual:
El vocabulario de la bolsa de valores y la banca de inversión. 

1. Bear market / Bull market (Mercado bajista / alcista): 
- Un 'Bear market' es cuando los precios de las acciones caen. Un 'Bull market' es cuando suben. 
Ej: Investors lost millions during the BEAR MARKET of 2008. 

2. Blue-chip stock (Acción de primera línea): 
- Acciones de empresas gigantes, estables y seguras (como Apple o Coca-Cola). 
Ej: She only invests her retirement money in BLUE-CHIP STOCKS. 

3. Dividend (Dividendo): 
- Una parte de las ganancias de la empresa que se paga a los accionistas. 
Ej: The company pays a quarterly DIVIDEND of $2 per share.
parts.audio: Welcome to Advanced Finance and Wall Street. Number 1: Bear market and Bull market. A bear market is a period when stock prices fall, and people are pessimistic. A bull market is when prices are rising. For example: Investors lost millions during the BEAR MARKET of 2008. Number 2: Blue-chip stock. These are shares in giant, financially stable, and reliable companies, like Apple or Coca-Cola. For example: She only invests her retirement money in BLUE-CHIP STOCKS. Number 3: Dividend. A sum of money paid regularly by a company to its shareholders out of its profits. For example: The company pays a quarterly DIVIDEND of $2 per share.

parts.visual:
4. Bailout (Rescate financiero): 
- Cuando el gobierno da dinero a una empresa en quiebra para salvarla. 
Ej: The bank received a $10 billion BAILOUT from the government. 

5. Liquidate (Liquidar): 
- Vender todos los activos de una empresa para pagar deudas y cerrarla. 
Ej: The store is bankrupt, so they will LIQUIDATE all inventory. 

6. Capital gains (Ganancias de capital): 
- Las ganancias obtenidas al vender un activo (como acciones o casas) a un precio mayor del que costó. 
Ej: You have to pay a 15% tax on your CAPITAL GAINS. 

7. Venture capital (Capital de riesgo): 
- Dinero invertido en startups tecnológicas con alto riesgo pero gran potencial. 
Ej: The startup raised $5 million in VENTURE CAPITAL.
parts.audio: Number 4: Bailout. When the government or another organization gives financial assistance to a failing business to save it from collapse. For example: The bank received a $10 billion BAILOUT from the government. Number 5: Liquidate. To sell off a company's assets, usually to pay debts when closing down. For example: The store is bankrupt, so they will LIQUIDATE all inventory. Number 6: Capital gains. The profit earned from the sale of an asset like stocks or real estate. For example: You have to pay a 15% tax on your CAPITAL GAINS. Number 7: Venture capital. Money invested in new, risky startups that have high growth potential. For example: The startup raised $5 million in VENTURE CAPITAL.

questions.question: Prices are falling, unemployment is up, and investors are scared. We are officially in a ____ market. (Mercado bajista).
questions.explanation: Bear market = mercado a la baja.

questions.question: The economy is booming and stock prices hit record highs every day. It's a strong ____ market. (Mercado alcista).
Investors love this company because every three months it pays a large ____ to its shareholders. (Dividendo).
questions.explanation: Dividend = dividendo (parte de las ganancias pagada a los accionistas).

questions.question: Microsoft and Johnson & Johnson are considered ____-chip stocks because they are large, stable, and historically profitable. (De primera línea).
questions.explanation: Blue-chip stock = acciones de empresas gigantes y seguras.

questions.question: During the 2008 crisis, the US government had to give the banks a massive ____ to prevent a total economic collapse. (Rescate).
The company has failed. We must ____ our assets, sell the office furniture, and pay off our debts. (Liquidar).
questions.explanation: Liquidate = liquidar activos (vender todo para pagar deudas).

questions.question: I bought the stock for $10 and sold it for $50. I must pay taxes on my $40 capital ____. (Ganancia de capital).
questions.explanation: Capital gains = ganancias de capital (la diferencia positiva entre compra y venta de activos).

questions.question: Silicon Valley is famous for ____ capital, where firms invest millions in risky, early-stage tech startups. (Capital de riesgo).
A person who provides capital for a business start-up, usually in exchange for convertible debt or ownership equity, is an ____ investor.
questions.explanation: Angel investor = inversor ángel (invierte su propio dinero al principio de una startup).

questions.question: When a private company first sells shares to the public on the stock market, it is called an ____ (Initial Public Offering).
questions.explanation: IPO = Initial Public Offering (Oferta Pública Inicial).

questions.question: To bet that a stock's price will go DOWN, so you borrow shares, sell them, and buy them back cheaper later. This is called ____ selling.
questions.explanation: Short selling (o 'shorting a stock') = apostar en corto (apostar a que el precio caerá).

questions.question: A group of investments held by a person or a company is their financial ____. (Portafolio/Cartera).
To spread your investments around so you don't lose everything if one company fails. 'Don't put all your eggs in one basket.' This is ____. (Diversificación).
An asset that can be quickly converted into cash without losing value is a ____ asset. (Líquido).
questions.explanation: Liquid asset = activo líquido (dinero en efectivo o fácil de vender).

questions.question: A measurement of how much the price of a stock fluctuates. High ____ means it is very risky and jumps up and down. (Volatilidad).
To buy a controlling interest in another company is an ____. (Adquisición).
questions.explanation: Acquisition = adquisición (la 'A' en M&A - Mergers & Acquisitions).

questions.question: A loan taken out to buy property or real estate is a ____. (Hipoteca).
questions.explanation: Mortgage = hipoteca (la 't' no se pronuncia: MOR-gij).

questions.question: The percentage charged by a lender to a borrower for the use of money is the ____ rate. (Tasa de interés).
A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money is ____. (Inflación).
A prolonged period of economic decline, generally identified by a fall in GDP in two successive quarters, is a ____. (Recesión).
